run.title: Three White Lights
run.subtitle: Gauntlet Loop build run
run.waveName: Wave 5 — four merged fixes back under fresh critics, and the tuning audit that nothing yet enforces

blockers.title: Both S1 design questions ruled by the human
blockers.body: Growth coupling: e1rm.ts and its cancellation property are CORRECT and stay untouched — that was never the bug. The gap is that the nudge is a flat constant not coupled to training stimulus, so a primed tap is free and strictly dominant (200kg to 770.65kg over 30 sessions, a PR on 30 of 30). Ruled NOT to fix it now: it belongs to the fatigue/progression module, which does not exist yet, and a stopgap in the daily loop would be thrown-away work plus a constant to unpick later. Accessory day: LiftKind stays exactly three members matching real meet structure; accessory day pays Training IQ, the §2 currency that already exists for it, and nothing lift-specific — no bestE1rmKg write, no e1RM close-out.
blockers.consequence: §3.4 now carries the coupling as a stated requirement on the module that will own it, so it cannot be lost, and §11 records it as deferred-by-decision rather than left open — with the note that the loop growth curve is not a shipping progression model and must not be tuned as one. §3.2 carries the accessory boundary, enforced in code rather than by convention. The S1 builder was redirected mid-flight: pacing fix cancelled, scope now the blind-check fixes plus the accessory boundary, with tests pinning ACTUAL behaviour and pointing at §3.4 so the gap stays visible in the suite. The V1 wiring builder was told the close-out now has three honest states rather than two — confirmed, projected, and no e1RM at all.

blockers.title: Sixteen blind checks, and the pattern held to the end
blockers.body: Every one measured a proxy rather than the claim: a generator that never produced the failing case, a bound the unfixed behaviour already satisfied, a hash standing in for a picture, a max over a region that included pixels the player cannot see, a ratio cap that a WORSE artifact satisfied more easily. Six were caught only by mutation testing.
blockers.consequence: Mutation testing is now the default ask on every dispatch, and builders have started pre-empting it unprompted — one added a source scan because it worked out that unbranding a signature would be invisible to vitest. The harness itself is now in scope: evidence bundles stamp their commit and refuse to be graded stale, and the progress page says so when a named screenshot is missing.

blockers.title: Two agents died silently, and node_modules was found wiped
blockers.body: The result-card and shot-verifier agents both last committed three days ago and never notified — the same silent kill as the earlier spend-limit halt. Four commits of finished result-card work sat unmerged the whole time. Separately, node_modules/.bin was empty and the vitest package was gone, so the suite exited 216 with NO output at all, which reads like a code crash rather than a broken install.
blockers.consequence: Both recovered by hand: npm install restored the toolchain, 21 merged worktrees were pruned to free 2.2G, and the card work is merged at 1244 tests across 23 files. The lesson is that a silent agent death looks identical to a slow one, so unmerged branches need checking by commit age rather than waiting for a notification.

blockers.title: The app is playable, and the harness that proved it was itself blind
blockers.body: App.tsx imports LiftScreen and a rep can be played in the browser — the day-one Skia spike is gone. But the tool built to prove the lift animates heavier never decoded a pixel: it hashed file bytes and compared probe values produced by the code under test. Copying the light screenshots over the maximal ones, with both manifests untouched, still made it report that the maximal attempt animates heavier. A renderer that drew nothing would have passed it.
blockers.consequence: That is the twelfth check this run that could not fail if the thing it named were deleted, and the worst, because everything downstream trusted it — including a status report I had already given. The heavier-at-maximal claim now rests on a critic's own inspection of the crops, which is a different and real basis: bar bend 3 against 1, strain climbing 0 to 3 against flat 0, ascent 69 ticks against 38. A builder is making the tool decode pixels and adding mutants that freeze the sprite while leaving the bar-path trace live.

blockers.title: Both open design questions decided by the human
blockers.body: Attempt weight: the GDD's "drop down" option is removed — within a lift, attempts repeat or increase, never decrease, and the tension is rewritten accordingly. e1RM: Epley named specifically, one formula, Brzycki banned from the codebase.
blockers.consequence: The meet engine already enforced non-decreasing, so that decision cost no code. The Epley decision did: Brzycki was the fallback past the chart's coverage precisely because Epley steps DOWN there (chart 1.7422w at rep max 16 vs Epley 1.5500w at 16.5). Rather than ship a non-monotonic curve or keep a banned formula, the module now refuses past a 16 effective rep max — a real capability loss, spelled out in its header and enumerated in tests.

blockers.title: Run halted once on the subagent spend limit, now resumed
blockers.body: Six agents were killed mid-flight when the monthly limit was hit: two critics, the e1RM rework, and the fatigue, streak and sprite builders. No usable work was lost — neither partially-started builder had committed anything, and their worktrees were discarded.
blockers.consequence: Dispatch is working again. The queue resumed in priority order: close the e1RM send-back first, then grade the two modules that were merged but never judged. The art and UI half of the run still has not started.

blockers.title: Reference now exists for some bars; four of the five still have no artifact
blockers.body: Five reference files are committed. That unblocks the sprite craft bar, which is being graded against a native-resolution SNES sprite for the first time — every earlier pass reported it unverifiable.
blockers.consequence: The other four previously-unverifiable bars cannot be re-run: the result card, gym art, meet-day sequence and cut-ins are not built yet, so there is nothing to compare. Their references are staged. Two limits remain even then — the meet photos are stills, so meet-day tension's "judge pacing and sound" half stays unverifiable without video, and the scoresheet is a live in-meet attempt board rather than a published federation results sheet.

pieces.name: Foundation
pieces.bar: Not a GDD bar — infrastructure. Must render, screenshot, and test.
pieces.note: Expo + TS strict + vitest + Skia-on-web + Playwright screenshot harness all verified working end to end.

pieces.name: RPE → %1RM table
pieces.bar: Published RPE charts. Binary and testable — critic verifies against source values.
pieces.note: WINS ITS BAR after six rounds. The final critic re-fetched both sources live at the pinned SHAs and confirmed every sampled cell matches the bytes, that the one documented disagreement is real and exactly where the module says it is, that no export remains mutable, that no indexed read can leak undefined past a null check, and that the hot path is unchanged. It named two stale-prose residuals and explicitly said not to spawn a round for them — folded into this touch instead. The chart still cannot be checked against the RTS publication from here, and the module claims no more than that.

pieces.name: e1RM formulas
pieces.bar: Published e1RM formulas. Binary and testable.
pieces.note: THE MATH WINS ITS BAR. The critic verified the Epley divisor against published sources and a pinned third-party implementation, re-fetched both chart fixtures and confirmed every cell the boundary figures depend on, hand-checked all five worked examples and the crossover point, confirmed the curve is strictly increasing across the whole domain and that the refusal fires exactly where the chart’s coverage ends, and found no invented value anywhere. All seven §12.3 conditions clean. Its one finding was a false quotation of CLAUDE.md in the module header — correct that the quote was false, but wrong about how: git history shows the phrase WAS in CLAUDE.md when the builder quoted it, and I removed it two commits later without updating the quotation. My staleness, not a fabrication. Fixed by quoting the rule as it now stands, verified verbatim against the flattened file.

pieces.name: DOTS scoring
pieces.bar: Published DOTS coefficients. Binary and testable.
pieces.note: WINS ITS BAR — the only piece to be graded and pass. All ten coefficients verified by the critic against source bytes it fetched itself from OpenPowerlifting, term order checked by hand two ways. Noted gap: no test pins any DOTS value to anything outside the repo, so a wrong digit at authoring time could not fail the suite.

pieces.name: Meet engine
pieces.bar: Meet structure correctness: order, 3 attempts, non-decreasing weight, best-per-lift total, bomb-out.
pieces.note: Structure WINS ITS BAR. Rework 5 merged: the rules-seal subsystem is gone — four constants, a unique-symbol brand, an error code, an exported check, four call sites, a 41-line essay and nine tests, including the BigInt re-derivation blind to the digits it was meant to check. Rules are now opaque behind a module-private symbol, so the tampering spread does not type-check, and the guard is proven by negative controls that revert it and confirm the directives go unused. meet.ts is 51 lines shorter and has no arithmetic left to get wrong.

pieces.name: Fatigue / readiness
pieces.bar: Plausible game-feel abstraction. No visible fatigue meter (§12.3).
pieces.note: PASSES ITS BAR. The critic had cleared the model and both live §12.3 refusal conditions, re-deriving the daily-vs-intermittent injury comparison by hand rather than taking the claim; what it sent back was two tests that could not fail if the behaviour they named were deleted. Both are now fixed and I re-ran the mutations myself rather than accepting the report: delete the technique-relief term and 1 test fails where 0 did before; delete physio shortening and 2 fail where 0 did. The technique test now pins the exact scaling across six ratings instead of asserting probability > 0, and physio is compared against the same duration roll unaided instead of restating a band the unaided value already satisfied. The third, weaker case was given real content rather than deleted, and the builder proved that by mutation too. Model untouched throughout.

pieces.name: Streak / Recovery Days
pieces.bar: Never punishes daily engagement. Manual token use, hold cap, first-break tutorial.
pieces.note: THE RULING LANDED AND THE INVARIANT HOLDS; THE RESIDUE DOES NOT. Arm-ahead is built: protection is armed by the session before an absence, the missed days consume it, and the whole offer/accept/decline surface is deleted. I verified the invariant independently — same training history across three app-opening schedules gives byte-identical results, so the outcome no longer depends on when the player looks. But the monotonicity residue SURVIVED, and the builder reported that rather than claiming the bar. I confirmed it and found the exact mechanism: trained {5,6,7} ends with balance 3 and the day-12 gap covered, streak 3; trained {0,5,6,7} ends with balance 1, the gap NOT covered, streak 0. Training day 0 opens a gap that consumes two Recovery Days which are then missing later — an extra training day converts idle days from FREE, no streak yet, into CHARGED, streak alive. So the cause recorded in §4.4 was wrong, and it was my analysis that put it there. Deleting the manual prompt was a clean test of that claim and the family did not move; Duolingo has the same property for the same reason. 36 inverting pairs over every 13-day calendar on currentStreak, worst deficit 3; the permanent record is nearly monotone at 5 pairs and deficit 1. The one change that would close it is Recovery Days ceasing to be consumed, which is a monetisation decision touching the hold cap, the earning table and §8.2 — correctly not built by a builder.

pieces.name: Tuning constants
pieces.bar: Every game-feel value a named constant in one place. Enforced by a magic-number audit.
pieces.note: PASSES ITS BAR, and it is enforcement rather than a document. The audit is DEFAULT-DENY and runs inside vitest: a numeric literal is a violation unless it sits in a top-level SCREAMING_SNAKE declaration in a registered constants home. Both halves are load-bearing — naming alone is not enough, because a component declaring its own named constant still fails the one-place test. No .tsx file may ever be registered, asserted. I verified it bites independently rather than taking the builder proof: planting REST_FADE_MS = 420 in RestView.tsx — correctly named, wrong place — fails with file, line, column and enclosing declaration. The ruling on one module or four: six feel homes stay put, unified by ONE REGISTRY cross-checked in both directions, so a tuning home cannot exist without being reachable from the index and the index cannot name a non-home. Physically merging ~4000 lines was rejected because spriteTuning is loaded by the offline sprite tool and would drag the session copy strings in. 36 findings fixed, including a whole StyleSheet of bare numbers in ResultCardScreen and the RGBA8888 byte layout written out four times, twice inside components. The builder wrote its own comment/string stripper because the existing one did not know what a regex literal was, and asserted length-preservation across every real file so a scanner bug that ate code could not make the audit silently blind. ONE REAL DEFECT I found on merge and fixed: the walk started at the repo root and descended into .claude/worktrees/, which holds COMPLETE SECOND CHECKOUTS, so it audited other agents in-progress copies — 24 findings, all in code already fixed here. Worse than false positives, because the verdict then depends on who else is building. Excluded with a test pinning it, and that also explains a spriteMarks failure in the same run as resource contention rather than regression.

pieces.name: Progression boundary
pieces.bar: No client-authoritative progression writes. Shaped for Edge Functions.
pieces.note: PASSES ITS BAR. The write side already won; the read side now has consumers, and the builder did not just add callers — it removed the bypass. There is no ServerRecord in useSession any more and no accessor for the row, so reaching for the wrong source does not typecheck because the wrong source is gone. All seven accessors went from ZERO non-test callers to real ones. I verified in the browser myself, 25/25 against the running app: server 196.1 on screen against the client own projection of 208.6, PR gold following the server from rgb(255,215,94) to rgb(232,236,244), a refused proposal showing the last confirmed 200.0 rather than the discarded 208.6, and accessory day rendering NO e1RM node at all with an em dash rather than a zero. It also found that projected was UNREACHABLE code before this — the old path proposed and settled inside one state updater, so pending existed as a local variable and never as rendered state, which means a renderer handling that branch would have been untestable decoration. Fatigue narrowed rather than documented: the brief carries exactly one field behind a compile-time allowlist, pruned to §3.4 horizon. Disclosed weakness: the browser verification is not wired into the suite, so a regression there is caught only by running the tool.

pieces.name: Lift input mechanic
pieces.bar: The lift must feel good (GDD pillar 1).
pieces.note: PASSES ITS BAR, and the brace gap is now closed too. The builder REFUTED the premise I passed it — rung 1 is not too strong for a static hold, it measured 48 silhouette and 252 changed body pixels of 1406 — and then found that the one-number fix I suggested would have made things WORSE: at any brace weight high enough to matter, the lifter popped back to rung 0 on the first tick of the descent, visibly loosening the instant the bar moved. So it moved BRACE and DESCENT_TOP together to 0.42, arguing the brace IS the top of the descent held still, and swept at 0.01 to avoid three values where a rung crossing lands on a depth-step boundary and silently costs a drawing. Brace strain is now 0 for light and 1 for both the default and maximal, and the light brace still reads unstrained. Motion channels byte-identical. Its mutation fails five tests with the pixel check failing at literally 0, not a shrunken number. It also noticed it was editing a constant that exists in TWO files and added a cross-file assertion that they agree, which nothing had enforced.

pieces.name: Lifter sprites & animation
pieces.bar: Blind A/B against real 16-bit sprite work — NOW GRADEABLE, reference committed.
pieces.note: REBUILT SO THE REFERENCE IS ACTUALLY READ, and the circularity is not merely closed but demonstrated. Every reference figure is now computed from sprite-ref-1 pixels at test time; swapping the file fails 11-12 tests and a blank PNG fails 11. The decisive demonstration: running the OLD colour-keyed procedure on OUR sprite, which is unarguably keylined, scores it CLEANER than the unkeylined reference — 0.61 percent interior keyline against 2.79 — so that mask was never measuring outlines. The new check reads the pixel outside the material only where the pixel beyond THAT is lit, so black crowd cannot pass as a drawn outline: reference 20.0 percent of 45 lit crossings, ours 89.7-97.3 across 448 frames. The two contradictory MEASURED figures are resolved — computed upper mean luma 137.99, comment A off in its split, comment B off by 17.4 percent and reproducing nothing. Limb checks now measure limbs, and mutating the head fails ONLY head checks while no whole-figure test moves, which is the point. It hit the exact false-pass trap the brief warned of and reported it: mutating edgeIndex alone changed zero pixels because edgeFollowsLight makes the field dead. New and genuinely objective: era conformance against the SNES 5-bit colour lattice, which I verified myself — ref-1 is 94/94 colours and 100.00 percent of pixels, the negative control 6/194 and 3.29 percent, so the baseball image cannot be a 16-bit game because its colours do not fit the hardware. Render byte-identical. Fresh critic dispatched on regenerated frames.

pieces.name: Gym / environment art
pieces.bar: Blind A/B, same era. Readability at phone scale.
pieces.note: Reference unreachable — bar will report unverifiable.

pieces.name: Daily session loop
pieces.bar: Duolingo-class session. Time-to-first-input, session length, close-out moment.
pieces.note: REWORKED AND MERGED after the human ruled the pacing fix out of scope. Nothing of the cancelled work landed — no pacing constant, no growth cap, no ledger coupling, no e1rm.ts change. What shipped is the checks and the accessory boundary. The 19th blind check is closed: the sweep that ran 685 iterations entirely at the one readiness where the ratchet is arithmetically impossible now runs 2740 cells across four bands, and each row asserts its fixture actually LANDS in the band it is filed under — grinding 0/685 above, steady 0/685, ready 634/685, primed 685/685. A second test drives 30 sessions through the public API and pins the 200-to-770.65kg curve with a comment naming the §3.4 dependency as recorded rather than endorsed. The builder proved blindness directly rather than asserting it, with five paired runs showing the old check green and the new one red under the same mutation; the sharpest is the session-length floor, which went red when the GUESSED pad shrank while the loop was unchanged — proof it measured the pad, not the session. It also found a LIVE RUNTIME HOLE while fencing accessory: such a session was being accepted, the streak advanced, a fatigue row written under lift accessory, and bestE1rmKg came back undefined while typed number|null, surviving only because estimate > undefined is false. Now fenced at compile time and refused at runtime. Honestly disclosed a disagreement with my own cited figure: 54.3s measured against the 58.7s browser walkthrough.

pieces.bar: Dread and anticipation comparable to a real third-attempt walkout.
pieces.note: Broadcast footage unreachable — bar will report unverifiable.

pieces.name: Result card
pieces.bar: Would a competitive lifter believe ours is real? vs. real federation sheets.
pieces.note: PASSES ITS BAR, and the eighteenth blind check is now closed. The test named leaves the grid, the total and the barbell exactly where they were compared ONE row — strip bottom 73 against grid header 74, so the loop ran once over a blank gutter. It now compares rows 73 to 239 inclusive, full width: 167 rows, 32064 pixels, and THAT COUNT IS ITSELF ASSERTED, which is the assertion the old one-row loop would have failed. The builder had to build the fixture rather than tweak one, and measured why nothing weaker works: at CONTENT.W 180 the masters phrase renders 217px and wraps, changing the division alone still gives 190px and still wraps, so only Raw / Open at 152px produces a genuine one-line twin. Both halves report the same total, DOTS and placing, hand-written in the test so a zero pixel diff cannot be two cards agreeing about nothing, and the attempts are retyped rather than shared with sampleCards so sample drift makes the pair disagree out loud. Six layout constants moved one at a time, all six caught. Crucially the builder noticed the diff alone could not catch them — moving a constant moves BOTH cards and the diff stays zero — so it also mutated the renderer to move the total block on the one-line card ONLY, which is the shape the A/B half exists for, and that failed correctly. It disclosed one surviving mutation rather than hiding it: spilling the second meta line out of the strip passes, because drawGrid repaints those rows afterwards, so the A/B half real coverage below row 74 is narrower than its framing suggests. It also flagged that hand-written absolute row pins mean the coming 30-iteration tuning pass will see test failures rather than screenshot differences. Typography remains UNVERIFIABLE for the fourth time — four hosts 403, confirmed by the critic itself rather than inherited.

pieces.name: Cross-module inconsistency (found, unfixed)
pieces.bar: The four modes must feel like one game — the smoothing-pass concern.
pieces.note: FIXED, and the fix chose refusal over conversion for a reason I checked and agree with. The unit now travels with the reading and dots.ts refuses a total it cannot prove is kilograms. I re-ran my own probe — the exact call that printed 806.45 — and it now refuses with a RangeError, while the same meet honestly declared in kg still scores 365.76. Better than the brief asked: a reading with NO unit is ALSO refused rather than defaulting to kg. POUND_MEET_RULES still validates, so pound meets remain runnable; they just cannot be DOTS-scored without an explicit two-call conversion. Why refuse rather than convert, which is the good part: a DOTS score needs TWO numbers in kilograms, and while the total now arrives with a unit, the bodyweight arrives from the caller as a bare number that no module produces. Converting the total while trusting the bodyweight turns a 2.2x overstatement into a 2.2x understatement from a module now claiming to handle units — and the builder cited OpenPowerlifting own checker carrying exactly that warning, that international meets often weigh in in pounds but lift in kilos. Coefficients, numerator, domain bounds and Horner order untouched. It also confirmed the twentieth blind check by driving the old form under the same mutation: deleting meet.ts weight gate left the old assertion green at 37.17 while the new one goes red. Three of four lesser findings closed, one disclosed. The required unit field on MeetLoadingRules is a breaking change, but a compile error rather than a silent one, and the builder trial-merged T1 before reporting.
